key_insight: A hybrid quantum-classical workflow can solve utility-scale Maximum Independent Set instances exactly by combining variational circuits, graph preprocessing, and strong post-processing.
engineering_relevance: The paper shows that near-term quantum algorithms can be made more practical for large combinatorial optimization through depth reduction, optimizer choice, and initialization strategies that improve scalability and hardware transfer.
method: Use VQE/QAOA with SPSA or COBYLA across multiple circuit depths.
Preprocess graphs with Fiedler-vector reordering and distance-based sparsification to reduce circuit depth.
Apply history-guided bitstring correction and maximality extension; for the hardest case, use ancilla-assisted superposition initialization with an excitation-preserving ansatz.
evidence_signal: Across 64-, 99-, and 180-vertex benchmark graphs, the approach recovers the exact MIS; CVaR-VQE with SPSA finds multiple distinct MIS per run, and the 180-node instance reaches optimality where standard methods stalled at size 14.
watch_item: Performance depends on careful preprocessing and post-processing, and hardware results may still be sensitive to noise, optimizer trajectory, and problem-specific initialization quality.
paper_title: Quantum Variational Approaches to the Maximum Independent Set Problem at Utility Scale
